logicalBugs.explanation: In a Gitea pull request (a proposed code change), open Files Changed for the latest single commit and submit text from its enabled Review panel. No review is posted: a technical error appears, the page remains on the commit-specific view, and the draft stays in the panel instead of completing the offered review.

rootCause.explanation: The latest-commit diff qualifies as IsShowingAllCommits, enabling the review form. That form appends /reviews/submit to .Link, which on the commit view includes /commits/<sha>; only the PR-scoped review route exists.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In a Gitea pull request’s latest single-commit Files Changed view, open the enabled Review panel and submit a comment. The submission fails at a nonexistent commit-specific endpoint and posts no review, rather than completing the offered review action.

sourceBugs.name: Review submission from the latest single-commit PR view fails with HTTP 404

reproductionPaths.expected: Submitting an enabled review from the latest/head single-commit PR diff should post the review successfully through the canonical PR review-submission endpoint.
reproductionPaths.actual: The review is not submitted. A raw JSON parse error banner appears, the page stays on the commit-filtered URL, and the text remains in the panel.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and create or use a PR whose latest/head commit can be selected from Files Changed.

logicalBugs.explanation: In Gitea, issue and pull request (a proposed code change) form actions can expose a raw JSON-parsing SyntaxError labelled Network error when the server rejects an unavailable or unauthorized action. Confirmed triggers include stale deleted/locked/archived comment or issue (a tracked work item) forms, deleted milestone (a named group of work items)/time-entry targets and rejected review actions; the UI does not explain the actual refusal.

rootCause.explanation: fetchActionDoRequest unconditionally calls resp.json() for HTTP 4xx and labels parsing exceptions Network error. Plain-text missing-issue/permission responses therefore expose SyntaxError rather than the rejection reason. Deleted comment inline edits use a separate parser and are kept separate.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In Gitea, a failed Review-panel submission receives a plaintext HTTP 404, but the UI labels a resulting client JSON parse exception as a network error.

sourceBugs.name: Review submission HTTP error is mislabeled Network error and exposes a JSON SyntaxError

reproductionPaths.expected: When Review submission receives an HTTP error, show understandable submission-failure feedback and preserve the draft. Distinguish an HTTP rejection from a network outage, and do not expose an internal JSON parser exception.
reproductionPaths.actual: The server responds HTTP404 with plain text Not found. The banner says Network error followed by SyntaxError: Unexpected token N / Not found is not valid JSON. The review draft remains in the panel.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and open a PR’s latest/head single-commit Files Changed view, where Review is enabled.
Open Review, enter a unique comment, and click Comment.
Observe the red banner combining Network error, SyntaxError and invalid JSON details. The request reached the server and received HTTP404; it was not a transport failure.

rootCause.explanation: SearchRepositoryCondition admits owned organization repositories and checks actor access with unit.TypeInvalid. The Issues UnitType does not constrain those repositories; dashboard search then loads their issues without per-issue unit authorization. Both disabled trackers and teams with Issues No Access pass this same repository selection.

rootCause.explanation: Indexer conversion copies Issue.AssigneeID, a nonpersisted legacy field, instead of Issue.Assignees. Specific, self and any-assignee filters therefore query incorrect indexed data. Non-keyword database filtering uses issue_assignees and succeeds.

logicalBugs.explanation: In Gitea, bulk Open can reopen a pull request that the pull request detail page refuses to reopen, including when its head branch is deleted or an identical pull request is already open. The bulk/API path leaves an invalid open pull request or duplicate open pull requests (proposed code changes) instead of enforcing the detail page’s refusal.

rootCause.explanation: The bulk issue status handler invokes ReopenIssue directly. It omits the detail-page checks for an existing identical open PR and a usable source branch, allowing invalid duplicate or broken reopen states.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In Gitea, bulk Open reopens a closed pull request after its head branch is deleted, bypassing the detail page’s explicit reopening prohibition and leaving a broken open pull request.

sourceBugs.name: Bulk Open reopens a closed PR whose head branch was deleted, leaving it broken

reproductionPaths.expected: Bulk Open must enforce the same deleted-head restriction as PR detail: keep the PR closed and explain that its deleted branch prevents reopening.
reproductionPaths.actual: The detail page says the PR cannot be reopened because its branch was deleted and offers no Reopen control. Bulk Open nevertheless persists an Open state and reopened event; the resulting detail page reports missing fork information and offers no merge control.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and create a disposable open PR with its own head branch.
Close the PR, use Delete Branch, and confirm deletion. On the PR detail, confirm the deleted-branch notice and absence of a Reopen control.
Open the repository Pull Requests list, select Closed, select the PR’s checkbox, and click bulk Open.
Open the PR detail again. It is now Open with a reopened event, but its merge box says This pull request is broken due to missing fork information and has no merge control.

rootCause.explanation: The compare GET checks for an existing branch pair, but the web create POST does not revalidate uniqueness at the mutation boundary. Two forms can therefore create the same open head/base pair.

logicalBugs.explanation: In Gitea, immediately after Update branch by rebase, the pull request's +/- totals beside the tabs include changes from the base branch (for example +3 -1 instead of +2 -1). Files Changed shows the correct totals, and the Conversation page corrects itself after navigating away and back.

rootCause.explanation: Candidate timing mechanism: Update defers a goroutine calling AddTestPullRequestTask, and UpdatePullRequest redirects after a fixed one-second sleep. GetPullDiffStats calculates against pull.MergeBase plus the current head ref, so a stale merge-base can include base changes after rebase until the check updates it. The source establishes asynchronous scheduling and the stat inputs, but the report-specific stale merge-base/read interleaving has not been traced.

sourceBugs.name: Pull request diff totals overcount right after Update branch by rebase

reproductionPaths.expected: After a rebase update, the pull request's +/- totals count only its own changes against the current base, matching Files Changed.

reproSteps: Open a pull request that changes one file, and note its +/- totals.
Add a new file to the base branch so the pull request is out of date.
Choose Update branch by rebase and run it.
Compare the totals shown right after the update with Files Changed, then return to Conversation.

logicalBugs.explanation: In Gitea, if a pull request's diff had become empty against its old base and it is then retargeted to a branch where it does add changes, the merge panel keeps saying 'The changes on this branch are already on the target branch. This will be an empty commit.' while Files Changed shows real changes. The empty status from the old base is never cleared when the target changes; merging still works.

rootCause.explanation: ChangeTargetBranch calls testPullRequestBranchMergeable on the existing PR without first replacing its Empty status with Checking. For a successful nonempty three-way merge, checkConflicts sets Empty only when the resulting tree equals the base and otherwise leaves the prior status unchanged. testPullRequestTmpRepoBranchMergeable then returns early whenever pr.Status is still Empty, before its final Mergeable assignment. ChangeTargetBranch only promotes Checking to Mergeable, so the old Empty value is persisted after a nonempty retarget.

rootCause.explanation: The code-comment form checks Required/nonempty rather than trimmed content and CreateCodeComment persists that content. This path does not use SubmitReviewForm.HasEmptyContent’s trim-based review-body validation.

logicalBugs.explanation: In Gitea, a newly requested reviewer can see a pull request (a proposed code change) in Review requested without a keyword, yet a matching title search hides it on repository or global pull request lists. Removed requests can likewise remain in keyword results; posting an ordinary comment makes the keyword filter catch up.

rootCause.explanation: Request-review mutations emit a notification whose indexer implementation is inherited as a no-op. Requested reviewer IDs are rebuilt only during a later issue reindex such as an ordinary comment.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On a Gitea repository's Pull Requests list, combining a text search with Type → Review requested shows No results, even though a matching pull request requests your review. Requesting a reviewer never refreshes the search index, so the search doesn't know about the request; Review requested without a search works.

sourceBugs.name: Repository Pull Requests 'Review requested' with a search hides a pull request awaiting your review

reproductionPaths.expected: A pull request that requests your review and matches the search stays listed when Review requested is combined with the search.
reproductionPaths.actual: Searching for the pull request's title listed it, but choosing Review requested with that search showed No results with 0 Open and 0 Closed. Review requested without a search listed it, and posting a comment on the pull request made the combined search find it.
reproSteps: Open a pull request and request another user's review.
As that user, open the repository's Pull Requests list and search for a word from the pull request's title; confirm it's listed.
With the search still applied, choose Type → Review requested.
Check whether the pull request is still listed, then clear the search and compare.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On Gitea’s global Pull Requests dashboard, request a user’s review and then use a matching keyword under Review requested as that user. The request is visible without the keyword, but the same pull request is omitted when the matching text search is added.

sourceBugs.name: Global Review requested omits pull request pending alex's review

reproductionPaths.expected: A matching keyword narrows the current reviewer-filtered list without hiding a qualifying PR.
reproductionPaths.actual: Fresh PRs awaiting the viewer’s review appear without a keyword but disappear with a matching title keyword. Numeric search works; posting an ordinary comment refreshes the index and restores results. Removed requests can remain in keyword results.
reproSteps: Create two fresh PRs authored by a user other than the reviewer.
Request the reviewer through the PR sidebar after creating each PR.
As the reviewer, open global Pull Requests → Review requested without a keyword and confirm the PRs appear.
Enter a matching title keyword and observe the missing PRs.
Clear the keyword as a control, then post an ordinary comment on one affected PR and confirm keyword results recover for it.

logicalBugs.explanation: In Gitea, when a pull request's changes are already on the target branch, the merge box says it will create an empty commit and still offers squash merging, but Create squash commit fails and the pull request (a proposed code change) stays open. The squash step commits without allowing an empty commit.

rootCause.explanation: doMergeStyleSquash invokes git commit without --allow-empty although the merge UI permits an empty commit. Git rejects the no-change commit; the generic merge server-error path yields only HTTP 500 feedback. The operation failure and opaque feedback share this reproduction trigger.

logicalBugs.explanation: In Gitea, for a pull request (a proposed code change) title near the 255-character limit, clicking "Add WIP: prefix" silently cuts the end of the title to make room, and "Remove WIP: prefix" can't restore it. No error or notification tells the user the title was shortened.

rootCause.explanation: The client prepends WIP to the existing title and posts it without a length check. ChangeIssueTitle uses EllipsisDisplayString(...,255), silently replacing the end of the saved title rather than rejecting the oversized edit.

rootCause.explanation: Code comments are associated with their stored TreePath and the diff/comment loading path does not remap that path through later Git renames. Threads remain attached to the old path even when outdated comments are shown.

logicalBugs.explanation: In Gitea, on global or organization Issues and Pull Requests, selecting an Author or Assignee and then clicking Open, Closed or an ownership sidebar link drops that user filter. Results and counts broaden to records excluded by the previously selected author/assignee, including when the ownership link was already active.

rootCause.explanation: The dashboard builds $queryLink without poster or assignee, then uses it for ownership and Open/Closed links. $queryLinkWithFilter contains those fields but is only used by the filter and sort controls. Global and organization dashboards share this template.

logicalBugs.explanation: In Gitea, set or change an issue (a tracked work item) or pull request’s due date in its sidebar, then search for matching text and sort by Nearest or Farthest due date. Global searches, and the repository issue-search path, can display the new dates but order results using earlier dates or as if no date were set. Posting an ordinary comment on the affected work item makes the search order catch up.

rootCause.explanation: UpdateIssueDeadline updates the database and timeline only; indexerNotifier has no due-date change hook. Keyword searches sort the indexed DeadlineUnix from the last indexing job until another supported notification reindexes the issue.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In Gitea, change a pull request’s due date from its sidebar, then use a matching text search and due-date sorting on the global Pull Requests dashboard. The row shows the new date while its position still reflects the previous saved date, instead of updating the search order.

sourceBugs.name: Global pull-request keyword search sorts by stale due dates after sidebar updates

reproductionPaths.expected: Nearest and Farthest due-date sorting on global Pull Requests uses current saved deadlines for matching PRs.
reproductionPaths.actual: With matching PRs due November 15 and December 20, Nearest due date can place December 20 first, and Farthest can retain an equally incorrect stale order. Reloading does not repair the ordering. Clearing the keyword or using the repository PR list sorts correctly. Posting comments on both PRs refreshes their index records and restores ordering; another due-date-only edit can break it again.
reproSteps: Create two disposable pull requests whose titles share a fresh nonnumeric search prefix.
Set their due dates from the PR sidebar, giving the older PR an earlier date and the newer PR a later date.
Open global Pull Requests, select Created by you and Open, search for the prefix, and choose Nearest due date.
Observe the later-dated PR listed above the earlier-dated PR. Reload and compare Nearest/Farthest ordering against the displayed saved dates.
As controls, clear the keyword or use the repository PR list and confirm current-date ordering.
Post a normal comment on each PR, repeat the global keyword sort and confirm it recovers. Change only a due date and check for stale ordering again.

logicalBugs.explanation: In Gitea, compare commits can call different branches equal when the selected head is an ancestor of the base. Reversing the comparison shows commits and a file diff, but the ancestor-to-descendant direction shows the equal-branches/empty-comparison message despite different trees.

rootCause.explanation: PrepareCompareDiff sets IsNothingToCompare when headCommitID equals the comparison MergeBase. This uses the empty base-to-head commit range from merge-base semantics as an equality test, although the selected branch trees can differ. Repository comparison and pull-request comparison share this decision.

analysis.explanation: Compare logic uses the base-to-head commit range and merge-base-oriented diff when the head is an ancestor of the base. That range contains no new head commits even though the trees differ, leading to the equal-branches empty display.
PrepareCompareDiff marks IsNothingToCompare when head equals MergeBase, using merge-base comparison semantics to display an equality claim even when the base has additional commits.

logicalBugs.explanation: In Gitea, a team can be asked to review a pull request (a proposed code change) on behalf of its members. rootCause.explanation: Issue index conversion adds Review.ReviewerID for requested reviews, without expanding ReviewerTeamID membership. A viewer’s team-only request therefore cannot match their user ID even after reindexing.

logicalBugs.explanation: In Gitea, after a pull request's source branch is deleted (for example by merging with Delete branch), the pull request's own page shows the branch name as plain text, but every pull request (a proposed code change) list (repository, global, organization, milestone (a named group of work items) and subscription lists) still shows it as a link, which opens a Page Not Found error. The list template always links the branch without checking whether it still exists.

rootCause.explanation: The shared issue-list PR branch markup constructs /src/branch/HeadBranch without the branch-existence guard used by the PR detail page. Deleted heads remain actionable links to 404 across list surfaces.
